summary: Intermittent ghost touchpad clicks on TPG-14 laptops after Windows 11 cumulative update
description:
Issue summary:
Users on TPG-14 v2 devices report intermittent 'ghost' left-click events after the Windows 11 cumulative update (KB500xyz) installed via WU on 2026-03-09. Ghost clicks occur while typing or when the palm rests near the touchpad; frequency varies but reproducible on affected hardware.

Impact:
- Several engineers reported spurious clicks causing accidental text selection, misplaced cursor actions, and interrupted builds.
- Affects day-to-day productivity for ~8 known devices in US-West office and a few remote users with the same SKU.

Environment:
- OS: Windows 11 22H2 (post-update state 2026-03-09)
- Devices: TPG-14 v2 corporate images (Autopilot-provisioned)
- Management: Intune + Autopatch for cumulative updates
- Region: prod-us-west

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot TPG-14 v2 with latest cumulative update installed.
2) Log into corporate profile (Intune policies applied).
3) Open VSCode or Chrome, type continuously and use touchpad to move cursor.
4) Occasionally observe a single left-click event without physical tap.

Observed logs / traces:
- Event Viewer (Windows Logs -> System) shows sporadic HIDCLASS warnings around the time of ghost clicks: "HID Input Driver reported unexpected input" (Event ID 1541).
- Device Manager shows HID-compliant touchpad driver version 3.2.1.45 (installed by Windows Update) whereas OEM driver previously was 2.9.0.12.
- ETW trace captured 2026-03-11 15:23 UTC shows an unsolicited input report from HID device 0x0A12 at the same timestamp as the user-observed ghost click.
- No blue screen or kernel dump captured; no consistent power state transitions.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced on two local TPG-14 v2 test units by installing the WU-provided driver (3.2.1.45). Reverted to OEM driver (2.9.0.12) and ghost clicks stopped during extended typing sessions.
- Checked Autopatch and Intune update rings: WU driver was pulled as part of the March cumulative on the Fast ring.
- Hypothesis: WU-provided HID driver introduces sensitivity change or misinterprets palm signals as discrete clicks under certain palm-rest electrical characteristics.
- Confirmed similar symptom referenced in vendor forum thread for a different OEM model after same WU package but not identical device.

Workaround applied:
- Rolled back driver to OEM 2.9.0.12 on 4 affected laptops and confirmed cessation of ghost clicks.
- Created an Intune temporary device configuration (script + Win32 app) to reinstall OEM driver and set a blocking policy for the WU driver version. Policy scheduled for cohort rollout tonight (2026-03-12 22:00 UTC) for all TPG-14 v2 devices.

Planned fix / next steps:
1) Push rollback package via Intune (Win32) for full fleet of TPG-14 v2 devices (deployment planned 2026-03-12).
2) Add a driver device configuration profile to block driver version 3.2.1.45 via Intune GPO equivalence until vendor releases a patch.
3) File upstream vendor SR with HID vendor and attach ETW traces + reproducer notes (ticket opened).
4) Update corporate imaging: bake OEM driver into the next image and modify Autopatch ring exclusions for the TPG-14 SKU until fix is released.
5) Monitor helpdesk queue for regressions for two weeks post-deployment and escalate if more devices surface.

Follow-ups / long-term:
- Vendor has indicated a potential fix timeline of ~2 weeks after triage.
- Engineering to consider a small telemetry datapoint to detect elevated input report rates near typing sessions (opt-in, privacy reviewed).
